newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo tea prices ease on low quality, big volume.
newsitem.headline: Colombo tea prices ease on low quality, big volume.

text.p: Prices fell at the Colombo tea auction, mainly because of lower quality and the huge volume on offer, brokers said on Wednesday.
"Low growns and high growns fell," said a Forbes and Walker broker. "Other than BOP fannings, most grades came down."
The anticipated gross auction average price for the six million kg on offer fell to 102.50 rupees ($1.77) per kg from 103.85 last week.
"We're still having huge sales," the broker said. "Also we're off the high grown quality season. That's one reason for high growns to drop."
The market should stabilise in the next few weeks with auction quantities dropping to around four million kg by the end of March, brokers said.
Select best Westerns BOP/BOPFs gained three to five rupees while other BOPs were down by three to five, Forbes and Walker said.
Among low grown teas, select best leafy teas were fully firm while others were three to four rupees lower, they said.
The next auction is on March 18-19, when 5.8 million kg will be on offer.
